captions.detailed: A perspective-control camera shift lens consisting of a dark, cylindrical outer barrel with ribbed grip rings and a light gray circular lens mount base at the bottom. The inner optical block is housed within the barrel, which connects to the mount via a sliding mechanism. This mechanical design allows the main barrel to shift prismatically perpendicular to the optical axis along a linear guide, and a rotation ring enables the shift direction to rotate relative to the mount.
captions.instruction: Generate a perspective-control shift lens assembly. The model should include a circular mounting base and a dark, cylindrical outer barrel with ribbed details. Integrate a revolute joint to allow rotation of the shift direction, and a prismatic joint to allow the lens barrel to slide laterally across the mount face.
captions.factory: Construct the model by defining three main parts: a mount base, a rotation ring, and a shifting lens barrel. Use Cylinder primitives to form the cylindrical bodies, and apply boolean subtractions to create hollow inner optical paths. Add ribbed details on the barrel using patterned boxes or polar arrays. Connect the mount base to the rotation ring with a revolute joint, and connect the rotation ring to the shifting lens barrel with a prismatic joint to represent the lateral shift mechanism.
